extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal funding (K-12 schools, postsecondary institutions), Title IX Coordinators, and institutional compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance on recipients' obligations under Title IX to provide information, supportive measures, voluntary leave, and reasonable modifications for students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions, and the Title IX Coordinator's coordination role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and effective response upon notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Title IX Coordinator is notified of a student's pregnancy or related conditions, the recipient always remains responsible for taking prompt and effective steps to prevent sex discrimination (e.g., provision of reasonable modifications, leave, and lactation space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must respond promptly and effectively under §106.44(a) and (f)(1) to concerns that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, including investigating complaints under grievance procedures (§106.45 and §106.46 where applicable) and, if discrimination is found, coordinating remedies and taking steps to ensure discrimination does not continue or recur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to provide information about recipient obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.40(b)(3)(i) requires the recipient to inform the student of the recipient's obligations under §§106.40(b)(1)–(5) and §106.44(j), in addition to the recipient's notice of nondiscrimination under §106.8(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing this information can be done in a single conversation or, where appropriate to the student's age and ability, by standardized written communication; the Department added the provision title 'Responsibility to provide information about recipient obligations' to assist readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to make reasonable modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.40(b)(3)(ii) requires a recipient to make reasonable modifications to its policies, practices, or procedures as necessary to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access to the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each modification must be based on the student's individualized needs; the recipient must consult with the student in determining necessary modifications; a modification that the recipient can demonstrate would fundamentally alter the nature of its program is not reasonable; if a student accepts an offered modification, the recipient must promptly and effectively implement it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive, individualized process for determining modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: When a student notifies the Title IX Coordinator of pregnancy or related conditions, the recipient must consult with the student to determine the student's individualized needs and offer options to prevent sex discrimination and ensure equal access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The student is not required to identify a specific modification; identifying a reasonable modification is a collaborative effort considering factors such as student age, type of program, health needs, and other circumstances (§106.40(b)(3)(ii)(A)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient bears burden to demonstrate 'fundamental alteration'
rubrics_metrics.description: A modification that a recipient can demonstrate would fundamentally alter the nature of its education program or activity is not a reasonable modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient has the burden of demonstrating that a modification fundamentally alters the program or is otherwise unreasonable. Case law in the disability context is illustrative (e.g., waiving essential academic or clinical requirements or jeopardizing accreditation tends to be a fundamental alteration). Even if a requested modification is shown to be a fundamental alteration, the recipient must still consult and offer other reasonable modifications that meet the student's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of reasonable modifications (non-exhaustive)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.40(b)(3)(ii)(C) provides a non-exhaustive list of potential reasonable modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include intermittent absences to attend medical appointments (with opportunity to make up lost class time), switching to a comparable later course section, make-up exams, tutoring or supplemental instruction, online instruction (not necessarily 'homebound'), providing larger desks, allowing lactation/bathroom breaks, allowing a student to sit or stand or carry water nearby, changes in course load, academic counseling, homework assistance, modification of uniform policies, and adjustments for athletic or extracurricular activities. Whether a particular modification is reasonable is fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between reasonable modifications and voluntary leave
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation to provide reasonable modifications under §106.40(b)(3)(ii) is separate and distinct from the longstanding obligation to provide voluntary leave under §106.40(b)(3)(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intermittent absences or other time off may fall under either framework depending on the circumstances; if a requested leave exceeds the framework in §106.40(b)(3)(iv), the excess should be treated as a request for a reasonable modification under §106.40(b)(3)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator coordination role and institutional responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient is ultimately responsible for implementing requests for reasonable modifications; the Title IX Coordinator is responsible to coordinate those actions and retain oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Title IX Coordinator may delegate specific duties to other offices (e.g., disability services, academic affairs, campus health) but must retain ultimate oversight to ensure consistent compliance under Title IX; coordination with Section 504 teams or IEP teams is appropriate where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion in offering reasonable options and student choice
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a range of reasonable modifications appropriate to a student's needs, the recipient may offer the full range or choose preferred options; the student has discretion whether to accept or decline an offered modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student declines an offered reasonable modification that would prevent discrimination and ensure equal access, the recipient is not required to determine or offer additional modifications for that specific need at that time, though it must offer and implement reasonable modifications if new or additional needs arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to offer alternatives when a requested modification is unreasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrating that a particular modification would be a fundamental alteration does not relieve the recipient of its obligation to consult with the student and offer other reasonable modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must engage in a good faith, interactive dialogue to identify modifications that meet the student's individualized needs and prevent discrimination, rather than simply denying requests without proposing alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-specific reasonableness determination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinations of whether a modification is reasonable must be fact-specific and individualized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the student has a preferred modification, whether alternative modifications exist, the feasibility and effectiveness of the modification in addressing the student's specific needs, and relevant programmatic constraints or academic standards; federal disability law jurisprudence is instructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with §106.44(g), the recipient must provide supportive measures, as appropriate, to restore or preserve access to the education program or activity in the absence of a complaint or while grievance procedures are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures may be necessary alongside or independent of reasonable modifications and should be timely and appropriate to the student's needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exhaustive and broadly inclusive list principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation's introductory phrase '[m]ay include but are not limited to' confirms that the examples of reasonable modifications are non-exhaustive and broadly inclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should not assume that options are limited to the listed examples; they may consider additional reasonable modifications (e.g., tutoring, supplemental instruction, changes in course load, or other measures suggested by commenters) tailored to individual students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger of obligations by notification (no student burden to propose solutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient obligations are initiated when the student or a person with a legal right to act on the student's behalf notifies the Title IX Coordinator of the student's pregnancy or related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The student is not required to identify or request a specific possible reasonable modification; the recipient must consult to determine individualized needs and offer options.
